$comment: The email list import's own steps (AGL-3671), contributed to the transferStep zone of the import wizard's review: whether the file may change the contact details of people already held, and the statement of permission under what the file holds. Each asks /api/transfer/plan again with its answer under extras['email-existing'] and extras['email-consent'], as the console's steps do. Grammar: docs/mobile/native-architecture.md §13.

screens.title: People already on this list
screens.subtitle: Whether the file may change their contact details

blocks.text: Somebody already on this list stays on it exactly as they are: the import never re-adds them or rewrites their membership. What the file can change is the contact record of people the workspace already holds — their name, phone, company and title.

fields.label: Update their contact details from the file
fields.help: Off: leave them as they are. The file’s contact details fill in only a contact the import creates. On: update their contact details from the file, under the field choices on the Conflicts step. A blank cell never empties one.

screens.title: Permission
screens.subtitle: The statement of permission, under what the file holds

blocks.text: This file looks bought or appended. Its columns include {data.screening.screening.purchaseTellColumns}. Purchased, rented and appended lists are not allowed, and importing one puts every site sending through this domain at risk. If the column name is a coincidence, carry on.

{data.screening.screening.roleAccounts:number} shared mailboxes. Addresses like {data.screening.screening.roleAccountSamples:first3} reach a mailbox several people read, or nobody. They are a common sign of a list built by collecting addresses rather than by people signing up. They are added if you go ahead.

blocks.title: Permission

items.label: I have permission to email everyone in this file
items.confirm: I have these people’s permission to send them marketing email, and I can produce the record of it if asked. This statement is stored against my account, with today’s date, on every address it admits.

items.label: Only add people who already have an opt-in on record

blocks.footer: Whichever you choose, people who unsubscribed, bounced, marked a message as spam or said no are never added, and an import never sends a confirmation email.
